# Versioned transactions and address lookup tables — facts

> Source-anchored units about Versioned transactions and address lookup tables: 26 across 9 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · 26 units · 9 sources · rights: quote -->

## Definitions

- [statement] A v0 message is a legacy message plus a 0x80 version prefix byte and an address_table_lookups array after the instructions. Each lookup names a table by its 32-byte address and lists one-byte writable and read-only indexes into it. The runtime appends the resolved writable addresses, then the read-only ones, to the static keys, and instructions index into that combined list. A lookup that selects no accounts fails sanitization. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://github.com/anza-xyz/solana-sdk/blob/master/message/src/versions/v0/mod.rs
- [statement] New table entries are not usable in the slot where they were added. The table stores last_extended_slot and last_extended_slot_start_index. While the current slot equals last_extended_slot, a lookup sees only the entries before that start index. A transaction that references a newer entry in the same slot fails. (high confidence) — https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx, https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs
- [statement] Do not catch -32015 and return null or 'not found'. It means the request failed on a versioned transaction, not that the transaction is missing. Helius says -32015 in logs already shows a project failing on versioned transactions. A payment-detection loop that swallows it reports a landed transaction as lost. (medium confidence) — https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/transaction-v1.md · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx, https://dev.to/timothymycompc/solana-rpc-error-32015-why-4-in-10-transactions-vanish-from-your-app-26cm

## How it works

- [statement] A lookup table holds at most 256 addresses (LOOKUP_TABLE_MAX_ADDRESSES = 256) because entries are addressed by a u8 index. A v0 message references a table by its address plus lists of one-byte indexes for writable and read-only accounts. (high confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html
- [statement] A lookup table is an on-chain account that holds at most 256 addresses (LOOKUP_TABLE_MAX_ADDRESSES = 256), because entries are addressed by a u8 index. A v0 message names each table by its address and lists one-byte indexes for the writable and the read-only accounts it loads from that table. ExtendLookupTable fails on a full table, on an extend that would pass 256 entries, and on a deactivated table. (high confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html, https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs
- [statement] Lookup tables supply only non-signer accounts. The fee payer and every signer stay in the static key list. Program IDs invoked by top-level instructions must also be static keys, because the v0 sanitizer rejects program ids loaded from lookup tables so programs can be analysed without chain state. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://github.com/anza-xyz/solana-sdk/blob/master/message/src/versions/v0/mod.rs
- [statement] Do not leave throwaway tables open. Tables never expire, and rent stays locked until the authority deactivates the table and later closes it. A bot that creates a table per route leaks rent unless it tracks and closes them. Rent must cover the table when it is created and after each extension. The Solana Foundation saw thousands to tens of thousands of tables created, extended or closed per day, so this churn is normal on mainnet. (medium confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/media/content/posts/transaction-v1-and-the-alt-trade-off.mdx
- [statement] Routers choose the version, not the bot. Jupiter /build: transactionVersion=1 forces v1 (default '0'). Jupiter /order: maxSupportedTransactionVersion=1 is only a ceiling, so v1 comes back only when Metis wins the route and the order is not gasless. Gasless and auto-sponsored orders are always v0, and the wrong parameter name is silently ignored. DFlow keeps v0 as the default and needs transactionVersion=v1 on /order and /swap. Branch on the version the response reports, and request v1 only for wallets that support it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/transaction-versions · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://pond.dflow.net/spot/trading/v1-migration-guide

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Addresses appended to a table are not usable in the slot they were added. The proposal says newly appended addresses need one slot to warm up, the program source says a table can only be used to look up addresses extended before the current bank's slot, and tutorials say to wait for the next slot after extend. A bot that extends and then immediately sends or simulates a transaction using the new entries will fail. (high confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-address-lookup-tables.md
- [statement] A deactivated table can still be used by transactions until its deactivation slot is no longer present in the SlotHashes sysvar. The table cannot be closed until then. The cool-down exists so in-flight transactions can land and to remove nondeterminism from loading addresses in the slot a table is closed. (high confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html
- [statement] The program source says it returns a generic error, not a specific one, for deactivated lookup tables, because a specific error would race with the table being closed at any point. A bot caching table accounts can therefore see a generic not-found style failure for a table that was deactivated, not a self-explanatory one. (low confidence) — https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables
- [statement] V1 keeps the per-transaction caps at 12 signatures, 64 instructions and 64 account addresses (255 account indexes per instruction); only the byte limit grows. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-15) — https://www.helius.dev/blog/agave-v4-2 · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables
- [statement] Limits the Anza proposal lists for v0 lookups: signers cannot be loaded through a table (full signer addresses stay in the message); hardware wallets cannot show details of accounts referenced through a table; only single-level lookups work; and a transaction may not load the same account twice, whether through account_keys or through a table. (low confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables
- [statement] Do not catch -32015 and report 'transaction not found'. Helius says that seeing -32015 in logs means the project is already failing on versioned transactions. One developer reports that batch reads (getParsedTransactions, getTransactions) throw for the whole batch when one entry is v1, hiding the other 49 transactions, and that apps returning null on the error mark paid transactions as missing. Older guides hard-code the old setting: OnFinality's lookup-table guide (undated) uses maxSupportedTransactionVersion 0 only, which now fails on v1 data. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-03) — https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/transaction-v1.md · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://dev.to/timothymycompc/solana-rpc-error-32015-why-4-in-10-transactions-vanish-from-your-app-26cm, https://onfinality.io/en/learn/solana-versioned-transactions-getblock-rpc
- [statement] FreezeLookupTable makes a table permanently immutable: it can never be extended or closed again, and its authority becomes none. Empty tables and deactivated tables cannot be frozen. A bot that depends on a third-party table can read the authority field. A frozen table can no longer gain entries or be closed out from under the bot. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/instruction.rs
- [statement] To move an ALT-based builder to v1, resolve each table entry, put the addresses inline in the single address array, and deduplicate them, because v1 rejects duplicates. Stay within 64 addresses and 4,096 bytes. Send transactions over 1,232 raw bytes as base64, since base58 stays capped at 1,232. v1 also defaults the compute-unit limit and loaded-accounts-data limit to zero, so set both explicitly (the compute-budget concept covers how). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/media/content/upgrades/larger-transaction-sizes.mdx · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-transaction-v1.md, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx, https://pond.dflow.net/spot/trading/v1-migration-guide
- [statement] A bot can cache a table's contents and re-fetch only to pick up new entries or to notice deactivation, meaning a deactivation_slot other than the maximum value in the table meta. Append-only entries and no re-creation at the same address mean a cached index never changes meaning. A cached copy that lacks a new entry cannot reference it, and a closed table makes the transaction fail. (medium confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html, https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The table authority must sign every extend, freeze, deactivate and close. Entries are append-only, so an index always resolves to the same address (Anza made tables append-only to stop front-running). FreezeLookupTable sets the authority to None; after that the program refuses extend, deactivate and close ('Lookup table is frozen'), so the table's rent is locked for good. A bot that depends on someone else's table, such as a router's, must expect the authority to deactivate and close it, and should re-fetch table accounts before building instead of caching them indefinitely. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Transaction signers may not be loaded through a lookup table; signer addresses must be serialized in full in the message. (low confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables
- [statement] A tutorial says creating a table costs about 0.003 SOL rent and each extendLookupTable instruction can add about 30 addresses (limited by transaction size), so filling a 256-entry table takes several transactions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-address-lookup-tables.md · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables
- [statement] Addresses appended to a lookup table are unusable in the slot they were added. The table records last_extended_slot and last_extended_slot_start_index; while the current slot is not past last_extended_slot, only entries below that start index resolve, so older entries keep working. A bot that extends a table and builds, simulates or sends a transaction with the new entries in the same slot gets a failed lookup (an out-of-range index, reported as InvalidAddressLookupTableIndex). Wait for the next slot. Each extend must also leave the table rent-exempt, so the payer funds the added rent. (high confidence) — https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs, https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-address-lookup-tables.md, https://github.com/anza-xyz/solana-sdk/blob/master/transaction-error/src/lib.rs
- [statement] Jupiter Swap V2 GET /swap/v2/build returns addressesByLookupTableAddress, an object that maps each lookup table address to its account array, so no separate RPC fetch of table accounts is needed. /build returns instruction objects, and the integrator assembles, simulates, signs and sends the transaction (v0 by default). maxAccounts takes 1 to 64 and defaults to 64. In Jupiter's docs, 'V1' in the migration table means Jupiter's old API version, not Solana Transaction V1. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/migration.md · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/reduce-transaction-size.md, https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/transaction-versions.md
- [statement] Tables are append-only. ExtendLookupTable adds entries and nothing removes or reorders them. The program rejects an empty extension, a full table, and an extension that would pass 256 entries, and only the table authority can extend. Entries are never rewritten, so an index that resolved to an address once resolves to it for the table's lifetime. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx
- [statement] Do not send value-moving transactions that depend on a table that is not yet finalized. The Anza proposal warns that an attacker could fork the chain just after a table is created and add a different entry in the fork. It advises waiting for the table to be finalized and optionally adding integrity-check instructions. Tutorials and the Solana docs example wait only one slot after an extend. (medium confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-address-lookup-tables.md
- [statement] Jupiter's current Swap V2 /build endpoint returns addressesByLookupTableAddress: the tables to compile against on v0, and an empty object on v1. The Metis Swap API page now carries a banner saying that API is no longer actively maintained and is superseded by Swap V2. Code copied from the older swap-instructions examples may therefore sit on a legacy path. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/transaction-versions · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/requote-with-lower-max-accounts
- [statement] A v1 transaction starts with version byte 0x81 at offset 0 and carries its signatures at the tail with no length prefix. Counts are fixed-width u8 fields, and instruction headers come before the payloads. Legacy and v0 start with a compact-u16 signature count; v0's 0x80 is the first byte of the message, after the signatures. A parser that expects a leading signature array fails on v1 bytes. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx · keywords: Versioned transactions and address lookup tables · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-improvement-documents/blob/main/proposals/0385-transaction-v1.md, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-transaction-v1.md, https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/transaction-v1.md
